issue.body:
Can rebuilding after historical resets restore correct-revision code without per-task repairs? Follow-up to #28, initially scoped to MACS; investigation remains open.

**Candidate evidence:** an opt-in hook replays recorded bootstrap commands after patch application in native validation and exported verification. Twelve compiled lifecycle checks, seven graded-export checks and six complete native-validator checks pass. The native check produces the expected F2P/P2P sets; pre/post build failures stop validation. Default-off outcomes and commands match upstream.

**Integration:** the complete patched upstream package loads configuration, constructs the registered pipeline, builds tasks and writes Harbor files for default/on/off settings. Missing rebuild commands and unknown options are rejected. No external calls occur in these checks. This is synthetic local evidence, not biological recovery or a full generation CLI/Docker/Harbor run; the dependency environment is recorded and is not upstream's full locked environment.

**Baseline result:** all 16 original MACS bootstrap actions replayed with their recorded exits, including syntax errors, without repairs. The following full-suite smoke check timed out at 300 seconds; the sandbox was removed before image commit or PR792 validation. Partial passing output does not establish completion. [Verified diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/7a5dac7f/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-replay-diagnosis.json).

**Remaining:** establish a faithful executable baseline before the original/candidate MACS comparison. Correct-revision compilation in a fixture does not prove historical dependency compatibility or task suitability. A separately checkpointed longer post-bootstrap-check allowance is the next timing comparison. One terminal replay used 0.94144 allocated CPU-hours within the 16-hour ceiling, zero model calls; archive readback and complete owned-resource cleanup are verified. No image is retained. Research only, nothing promoted to main.

[Native outcomes](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/native-outcome-results.json) · [Package integration](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/package-integration-results.json) · [Frozen MACS case](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-case.json) · [Full scope](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/issue-scope.md). Detailed logs remain in comments.

comment_body:
🤖 **The MACS reconstruction now reaches the original post-bootstrap smoke test.** All 16 recorded BASH actions matched their original exit codes, including the three syntax errors. No original command or dependency was repaired. The following full-suite smoke command then hit its unchanged 300-second limit. The timeout guard stopped further execution and removed the sandbox; image commit, fresh-image verification and PR792 validation were not reached.

[Stage diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/7a5dac7f/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-replay-diagnosis.json) · [Archive readback](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/7a5dac7f/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-recorded-readback-001.json). Partial output reached 86%; the pinned parser counted 4,333 passed and 249 skipped statuses. These are incomplete diagnostic counts, not a completed test suite or a validated task. The smoke command identity was verified against the recorded executor call.

One attempt used 0.94144 allocated CPU-hours; the 56,528-byte archive and output hashes are verified. All owned containers/images, checkout and downloaded tools were removed. Zero model calls. The first-stage ceiling remains 16 CPU-hours.

The next useful comparison is a separately checkpointed longer post-bootstrap smoke/fresh-check allowance, holding all recorded actions, source, test command and CPU/memory fixed. It has not been submitted or applied to this failed run. A retained executable baseline is still required before the frozen original-versus-rebuild PR792 comparison.
